29 September
On this day in 1690

Sahibjadha Baba Jujhar Singh Ji, son of Guru Gobind Singh, was born to Matta Jito

He fought valiantly in the Chamkaur battle and accepted shahidi in teh battle of Chamkaur on Dec. 22, 1704.

29 September brings together two moments of Sikh history, from 1690 to 1914. The main event of the day is from 1690: Sahibjadha Baba Jujhar Singh Ji, son of Guru Gobind Singh, was born to Matta Jito. Together they span two periods, from Guru Gobind Singh Ji and the Khalsa (1675–1708) to Colonial Punjab and the Singh Sabha revival (1850–1919). People, places and movements connected with this day include Guru Gobind Singh Ji, the Sahibzade and Chamkaur Sahib.

Historical background

Guru Gobind Singh Ji and the Khalsa (1675–1708)

Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji was executed in Delhi in 1675 on Aurangzeb's orders, and his son Guru Gobind Singh Ji became the tenth Guru at the age of nine. From Anandpur and Paonta he led the Sikhs through conflicts with the hill rajas and Mughal governors, created the Khalsa at Vaisakhi in 1699, and in the battles of 1704–1705 lost all four Sahibzade. Before his death at Nanded in 1708 he vested Guruship in the Guru Granth Sahib and the Khalsa Panth.

On this day in this period: 1690 Sahibjadha Baba Jujhar Singh Ji, son of Guru Gobind Singh, was born to Matta Jito.

Colonial Punjab and the Singh Sabha revival (1850–1919)

Under British rule Sikhs were recruited in large numbers into the army while new reform movements arose: the Namdhari (Kuka) movement, the Singh Sabha movement founded at Amritsar in 1873, the Chief Khalsa Diwan (1902), Khalsa College and the Anand Marriage Act (1909). The period ended with the Ghadar movement, the Komagata Maru episode (1914) and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 13 April 1919.

People and places of this day

Guru Gobind Singh Ji

The tenth Guru (1666–1708), born at Patna. He created the Khalsa in 1699, led the Sikhs through the battles of Anandpur, Chamkaur and Muktsar, composed works collected in the Dasam Granth, and before his death at Nanded vested Guruship in the Guru Granth Sahib.

Read more → · Mentioned on 24 other days of the year

The Sahibzade

The four sons of Guru Gobind Singh Ji. The elder two, Ajit Singh and Jujhar Singh, fell at Chamkaur in December 1704; the younger two, Zorawar Singh and Fateh Singh, were bricked in alive at Sirhind on the orders of Wazir Khan, an event remembered every December during Shaheedi Jor Mela.

Read more → · Mentioned on 7 other days of the year

Chamkaur Sahib

The site of the battle of December 1704 in which Guru Gobind Singh Ji, with forty Sikhs, held a mud fortress against a far larger Mughal force; the two elder Sahibzade, Ajit Singh and Jujhar Singh, fell here.
